purpose: Produce each completed in-memory module interface once at its checked-module boundary so importer operations do not rebuild all interfaces.
question: When should a same-process module interface be produced and how should finalization handle the interface collection?
decision: After checkModule completes a module body, TypeChecker builds and stores that module's interface from the graph snapshot and ModuleSymbols public records. Import and re-export consumers read the target record. Final buildModuleInterfaces only fills an absent record defensively and orders the module vector by moduleId.

production_contract.boundary: A module interface is produced after the module body and all recursively required dependency checks complete.
production_contract.identity: Graph-backed sourceId, canonicalPath, moduleId, entry status, and dependency edges are copied for the completed module.
production_contract.public_shape: Values, structs, enums, methods, generic metadata, resolved names, and receiver metadata are copied from ModuleSymbols.
production_contract.canonicalization: Values, structs, enums, and methods are sorted within the module at production time; finalization sorts modules by moduleId.
production_contract.fallback: Finalization may fill a missing module record while the checked-module invariant is still being migrated.

compatibility_boundary.imports: Direct, namespace, re-export, search-path, and cycle behavior are unchanged.
compatibility_boundary.diagnostics: Existing import, re-export, generic, and file-aware diagnostics retain their current tokens and messages.
compatibility_boundary.outputs: Module-interface text, AST, IR, bytecode, cdbc artifacts, runtime output, and Rust VM behavior are unchanged.
compatibility_boundary.persistence: Interface records remain snapshot-local in-memory data and are not serialized or used as persistent cache keys.
compatibility_boundary.producer: Dependency bodies remain the current same-process interface producer; M3B owns independent module results and dependency-body removal.

migration: Replace full-program rebuilds at import and re-export sites with completed-module production, retain final missing-record materialization during the invariant migration, and prove the recursive import/re-export chain with focused source-metadata assertions plus the full verification inventory.
quantitative_gate: The focused ir_source_location and module_interface_emitter CTests pass, verification_inventory validates 1,745 cases, and the full legacy, canonical, boundary, malformed, artifact, and Rust VM commands report zero unexplained differences.
old_path_deletion_condition: Remove final missing-interface materialization only after every graph module has a completed-module interface in the canonical inventory and two verification runs prove importer visibility from those records. Do not remove dependency-body checking or lowering here.
affected_consumers: TypeChecker direct, namespace, and re-export interface consumers
module-interface identity, dependency, ordering, and source-metadata tests
future independent module and cache-result production
out_of_scope: interface hashes, persistent cache keys, and invalidation
independent module checking and dependency-body deletion
per-module cdbc artifacts and linker/load rules

focused_commands: python3 tests/run_golden_tests.py ./build/compiler_design --case module_interface --case generic_imports --case generic_method_imports --case generic_struct_method_imports
